stem.evolab.island_hint_meadow: Mild weather and abundant food. Look for variation before changing anything.
stem.evolab.island_hint_snow: Pale coats blend into snow. More insulation helps in the cold.
stem.evolab.island_hint_drought: Food is scarce. Heavy insulation and long legs both carry energy costs.
stem.evolab.island_hint_forest: Dark coats are harder to spot. Longer legs improve escape but cost energy.
stem.evolab.island_scene: Living Island habitat. Use the organism selector below to inspect any creature.
stem.evolab.island_loading: Growing your island… You can already use every simulation control.
stem.evolab.island_fallback: Habitat map · 3D is unavailable on this device. All experiments and family records still work.
stem.evolab.island_camera_hint: Drag to orbit · tap a creature to meet it · pale rings mark your selection, gold rings its family
stem.evolab.island_quest_cold_question: Who leaves offspring when winter arrives?
stem.evolab.island_quest_family_question: How far will one spriglet’s family reach?
stem.evolab.island_quest_drift_question: Can traits change without an advantage?
stem.evolab.island_quest_intro: Choose a guided investigation or explore freely. Each uses your current population and holds the climate steady. Your island history stays with you.
stem.evolab.island_quest_unavailable_end: Start a new expedition below for another full investigation. Your existing evidence remains available to review and export.
stem.evolab.island_quest_unavailable_pas: Return to the present to start an investigation. You can still explore this recorded generation.
stem.evolab.island_quest_changed: Settings changed during this investigation. You can still record it as exploratory evidence.
stem.evolab.island_quest_extinct: The population ended early. Extinction is an observation: review the final survivors and record what happened.
stem.evolab.island_quest_ready: Your evidence is ready. Replay the result generation, then collect a field note. An unexpected result counts as a discovery too.
stem.evolab.island_quest_active: Follow the island through the next generations. Playback pauses when your investigation reaches its result.
stem.evolab.island_replay_wait: Advance once to reveal which parents survived and what their offspring inherited. You can replay the same evidence as often as you like.
stem.evolab.island_replay_parent_hint: These are the parents before survival was sampled. Their genes stay the same throughout their lives.
stem.evolab.island_replay_survivor_hint: These are the actual survivors, still in their original places. Everyone else left no offspring in this round.
stem.evolab.island_replay_child_hint: These are new individuals. Each inherited one allele per trait from each of two surviving parents.
stem.evolab.island_replay_dots: Each dot is one organism; the dark line marks the mean.
stem.evolab.island_replay_selection: Traits and chance both affected survival. The offspring mean can shift again through inheritance and random sampling.
stem.evolab.island_replay_neutral: Trait advantages were off. Differences here arise from random survival, inheritance, and any mutations—not a survival advantage for a trait.
stem.evolab.island_family_showing: Showing the first four. Explore the next generation for the rest.
stem.evolab.island_family_pending: This organism’s next generation has not been recorded yet.
stem.evolab.island_family_not_survived: This organism did not survive the next round. Its traits remain unchanged in the record.
stem.evolab.island_family_no_offspring: This organism survived but left no recorded offspring. Survival does not guarantee parenthood.
stem.evolab.island_family_trace_help: Choose a parent or offspring to visit its birth generation. Follow the same family as its traits are reshuffled.
stem.evolab.island_inheritance_trace_hel: The first allele comes from the first parent; the second comes from the second parent. A new value indicates a mutation during inheritance. Displayed values are rounded. Matching values do not identify which identical copy was inherited.
stem.evolab.island_quest_started: Investigation started with your current population. Living climate is off. Follow the generations, review the evidence, then collect a field note.
stem.evolab.island_quest_collected: Field note collected and saved to your Learning Journal. Try another question, or repeat with a fresh seed to test how reliable the pattern is.
stem.evolab.island_habitat_queued: Habitat changed. Run the next generation to test survival here. Living climate is now off so you can control this experiment.
stem.evolab.island_new_world_status: A fresh population is ready. Start by meeting a spriglet.
stem.evolab.island_prediction_saved: Prediction locked. Observe five more generations, then compare the evidence.
stem.evolab.island_arrival_story: 36 spriglets have arrived, each with a different mix of inherited traits. Meet one, make a prediction, then advance a generation.
stem.evolab.island_survived_story: survived to breed. Their offspring form the new generation. Parents keep their original traits.
stem.evolab.island_extinct_story: Fewer than two spriglets survived to breed. This population left no next generation. Rewind to investigate, or start a new expedition.
stem.evolab.island_finding_saved: Evidence saved to your Learning Journal. Add your explanation in the field note below.
stem.evolab.island_export_failed: The browser could not download this file. Use Save finding to keep the evidence in your journal.
stem.evolab.island_subtitle: Small creatures. Changing worlds. An evolutionary story you can follow.
stem.evolab.island_extinction: Your population went extinct. This is evidence to investigate, not a failed score. Rewind the timeline and inspect the last breeding generation.
stem.evolab.island_finished: 60 generations recorded. Your expedition is complete: explore the timeline, export your data, and explain what changed.
stem.evolab.island_remember_body: Each spriglet keeps the genes it was born with. Evolution appears across generations as different parents leave offspring. Walking and hopping are decorative; survival is calculated once per generation.
stem.evolab.island_log_founders: 36 founders. Three inherited traits. No two gene combinations are the same.
stem.evolab.island_log_climate: Living climate changed the habitat before this round of survival.
stem.evolab.island_climate_help: A fresh habitat every 5 generations. Turn off for a controlled experiment.
stem.evolab.island_motion_reduced: Your reduced-motion preference keeps the habitat still.
stem.evolab.island_survival_outlook: Model survival chance in this habitat
stem.evolab.island_tracking: Family tracking started. Gold rings mark this organism and its descendants.
stem.evolab.island_allele_help: One allele from each parent; the trait is their average. Values use a teaching scale from 0 to 1.
stem.evolab.island_meet_hint: Tap a creature on the island or choose one above. Inspect its coat, insulation, legs, and parents.
stem.evolab.island_family_help: A descendant may inherit no particular allele from a distant ancestor. Relatedness is not identical traits.
stem.evolab.island_chart_alt: Mean inherited traits across generations. Exact values are available in the generation table below.
stem.evolab.island_comparison: Founders compared with the generation you are viewing
stem.evolab.island_chart_help: Dashed vertical markers show habitat changes. These are population averages, not upgrades to individual creatures. A single run mixes selection and chance; repeat with fresh seeds to look for a pattern.
stem.evolab.island_prediction_question: Over the next five generations, what will happen to average insulation? Choose a habitat first. For a clearer test, keep Living climate off.
stem.evolab.island_prediction_extinct: The population went extinct, so there is no mean trait to compare.
stem.evolab.island_prediction_supported: This run supports your prediction. Could a different seed give a different result?
stem.evolab.island_prediction_not_suppor: This run did not match your prediction. Inspect who survived and what changed. Unexpected results are useful evidence.
stem.evolab.island_selection_off_help: Turn off for trait-neutral survival. Random survival, inheritance, and drift still occur.
stem.evolab.island_mutation_help: Mutation rates are deliberately exaggerated for a short lesson. New changes are random with respect to what the environment rewards.
stem.evolab.island_reset_help: Starting over replaces this island and timeline. Export your data or save a finding first. The same seed and the same actions reproduce the same result.
stem.evolab.island_model_title: How this world works · teacher notes
stem.evolab.island_model_body: Spriglets are fictional organisms in a simplified population-genetics model. Three independent diploid loci control continuous traits; one allele per locus comes from each of two randomly sampled surviving parents. The trait is the average of its two alleles. Survival depends on habitat, coat camouflage, insulation, leg length, food, and chance. Longer legs aid escape but cost energy. Mutations happen during inheritance, with no knowledge of the environment.
stem.evolab.island_model_limits: Generations do not overlap. At least two survivors are needed to breed. The next population has 2.65 offspring per survivor, rounded down and capped at 60. Carrying capacity, trait effects, and mutation rates are teaching choices, not measurements. The model omits migration, linkage, dominance, learned behavior, age structure, and reproductive isolation. It does not simulate the full evolutionary process or demonstrate speciation.
stem.evolab.island_teacher_prompt: Try a 10-minute investigation: inspect two founders; predict the effect of a long winter; hold that habitat for five generations; compare allele pairs in parents and offspring. Repeat with a fresh seed. Then disable trait-based survival to investigate drift. A single run cannot separate all causes of change.
stem.evolab.island_landscape_model_note: The scenery draws inspiration from Galápagos lava shores, arid scrub, and greener highlands. This is a fictional island, not a geographic replica. Winter is an experimental climate, not a Galápagos season. Terrain, plants, water, and scenic viewpoints are visual context: all spriglets experience the selected habitat, regardless of position. This tool follows inherited traits across generations; the Ecosystem tool explores interactions between species and resources.
stem.evolab.island_science_source: Science reference: UC Berkeley Understanding Evolution — mutations
stem.evolab.island_hero:
A small island.
An extraordinary story.
stem.evolab.island_hero_body: Meet the spriglets. Follow their families, change their habitat, and discover how a population evolves. Every generation has a story. What will yours reveal?
stem.evolab.island_hero_hint: No setup needed · 10-minute first expedition · new worlds to discover
stem.evolab.island_note_prompt: What changed in your population? Use a before-and-after number, explain inheritance and survival, and name one limit of this model.
